title: Violin study, playing by ear, and age at saxophone
summary: No musicians in his family; he studied violin about seven years but played by ear, and took up saxophone around 19.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well, to get back to the very beginning, were your family musical before you?

No. Nobody in my family played a musical instrument. I started in, I studied the violin. I actually studied violin for seven years. But I never could play the thing worth a nickel. I learned music, but I never could play the violin. I used to, one of, my main trouble was I wouldn't read music. I'd play the violin all right, but everything I was playing was being played by ear. And when Professor Shank, or Shrank, would come up to hear my lessons, he'd tell me point blank, you're playing by ear, you're not reading those music. And I'd tell him, yeah, that's a fact, I am playing by ear. I played the violin, as I said, the only time I ever played the violin was in that summer that we spent it across the lake when I became interested in the saxophone. And I picked that up without studying it.
How old were you when you started on violin?
Oh, on violin, I must have been about 16 years old. 15 or 16.
You started 15 or 16. Yeah. And, let's see, you took up saxophone when you were over there? How old were you when you crossed the lake?
Well, I must have been about 19 years old. That's,
that's about how old I was
when we were playing on the Gulf Coast.
So you were playing professionally in 1920 then?
